case_studies.title: Agent Safety Should Be a Runtime Contract
case_studies.abstract: The dominant paradigm treats AI safety as a property to be instilled during model training via RLHF, DPO, or Constitutional AI. We argue this is structurally insufficient for autonomous agents that execute code, mutate files, send messages, and modify databases. Agent safety should be a runtime contract enforced by the harness, and the contract has two complementary faces. The preventive face blocks dangerous actions before they happen via sandboxes, permission gates, output filters, and trajectory monitors. The evidential face requires verifiable proof that good actions actually happened, gat
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of ensuring AI safety in autonomous agents by introducing a runtime contract that enforces safety measures. The authors built a system with two complementary faces: a preventive face that blocks dangerous actions and an evidential face that requires proof of good actions. The result is a more robust AI safety framework.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure with autonomous agents, here is what to do: review your current safety measures, consider implementing sandboxing and permission gates to block dangerous actions, and set up monitoring to verify that good actions are being executed.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty: 10 - while not entirely new, the idea of runtime contracts for agent safety provides a fresh perspective. IT Relevance: 25 - the concept of agent safety affects how IT engineers design systems and implement safety measures. Value 90 Days: 10 - IT engineers could use this to propose additional safety measures, but the concrete implementation might take longer and depends on specific systems.

case_studies.title: AgentSOC: A Multi-Layer Agentic AI Framework for Security Operations Automation
case_studies.abstract: Security Operations Centers (SOCs) increasingly encounter difficulties in correlating heterogeneous alerts, interpreting multi-stage attack progressions, and selecting safe and effective response actions. This study introduces AgentSOC, a multi-layered agentic AI framework that enhances SOC automation by integrating perception, anticipatory reasoning, and risk-based action planning. The proposed architecture consolidates several layers of abstraction to provide a single operational loop to support normalizing alerts, enriching context, generating hypotheses, validating structural feasibility,
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of security operations centers struggling to correlate alerts and respond to attacks by introducing a multi-layered AI framework called AgentSOC. The framework automates security operations by integrating perception, reasoning, and action planning. It provides a single operational loop to normalize alerts, enrich context, and generate effective responses.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage a Security Operations Center (SOC), here is what to do: evaluate AgentSOC as a potential solution to automate security operations, assess its integration with your existing infrastructure, and consider implementing its multi-layered AI framework to enhance alert correlation and response actions.
case_studies.score_reasoning: High novelty in applying agentic AI to SOC automation, high IT relevance, moderate value to IT engineers and consultants within 90 days, but uncertain monetisation potential.

case_studies.title: SKILLER: Language-Level Reinforcement Learning for Reusable Skill Extraction in Small Language Models
case_studies.abstract: Agent skills represent a standardized format for packaging procedural knowledge and domain expertise, serving within agent harness systems as an essential mechanism to continually constrain a language model's behavior space for repeatable, high-quality task execution. However, because strong closed-source models entail high inference costs, current popular agent harnesses, such as Codex and OpenClaw, remain prohibitively expensive when deploying these skills to accomplish real-world tasks. The rapid capability enhancement of open-source models deployable on consumer-grade GPUs presents a compe
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of high costs associated with deploying agent skills in language models by building a system called SKILLER, which enables reusable skill extraction in small language models. The result is a more affordable and efficient way to deploy these skills. This is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on language models and agent harness systems, but IT consultants may be interested in the potential cost savings of using open-source models deployable on consumer-grade GPUs.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novel technique for reusable skill extraction, potential to improve performance and reduce inference costs. However, lack of specific deployment context or real-world examples in the abstract.

case_studies.title: An Agentic Workflow for Legacy HPC Modernization: Converting the Two-Electron-Integral Core of GAMESS
case_studies.abstract: Modernizing legacy Fortran is a problem of volume: the transformations are individually routine, but the codebases can be enormous, and across much of computational science the work simply goes undone. We propose an agentic workflow that takes this work on at production scale, and we set out to measure how far such delegation can reach. In this work, three prompt-specialized agent roles operate under a version-controlled specification that the agents themselves authored and revised, while humans hold a small number of gates. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of modernizing legacy Fortran code by creating an agentic workflow that automates the process, the team built a system where agents take on routine transformations, and the result is a scalable method for modernizing large codebases. This workflow allows for the conversion of legacy code to more modern and efficient languages. The outcome is a more efficient way to handle large-scale code modernization.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage legacy Fortran codebases, here is what to do: review your modernization efforts, consider implementing an agentic workflow, and assess the potential for automation in your code conversion processes. This flags a risk: if your organization relies on outdated Fortran code, check for potential security vulnerabilities immediately. Not directly applicable to general IT infrastructure work, but relevant to those managing HPC systems or legacy codebases.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty: An agentic workflow is mentioned, but not typically used in IT infrastructure; Relevance: HPC modernization is relevant, but not typically addressed by IT engineers; Value: A specific approach to modernizing legacy code could be useful, but depends on context.

case_studies.title: A Gateway Architecture for Enterprise MCP Authentication: Unifying Heterogeneous Auth, Identity Delegation, and the User / Non-User Persona Problem
case_studies.abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has become the de-facto interface for connecting LLM agents to enterprise tools, and adoption has been explosive: within a year, large organizations went from zero to dozens of internally built MCP servers. That speed created a governance crisis. Each team implemented authentication independently -- some with no auth, some with API keys, some with full OAuth -- producing a fragmented landscape with no consistent way to authorize callers, track who did what, or offboard a departing employee across the fleet. This paper reports an industry deployment that resolve
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of fragmented authentication in enterprise Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, by building a gateway architecture that unifies authentication, identity delegation, and user management. The result is a consistent and governable way to authorize callers and track user activity across the fleet. This improves security and compliance in large organizations.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage MCP servers, here is what to do: implement a gateway architecture to unify authentication and identity delegation, check your current authentication methods for consistency, and review your user management processes to ensure they are governable and compliant.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Paper reveals novel approach to MCP authentication, with industry-specific implications for IT engineers.

case_studies.title: Conversational Orchestration for Organic 6G
case_studies.abstract: The Organic 6G vision of a network of networks spanning an edge-cloud continuum complemented by non-terrestrial resources requires, to realize its promise, service provisioning that is simple to operate, scalable across independently administered domains, and agile under domain churn (i.e., domains dynamically joining and leaving). Despite advances in cross-domain orchestration, many proposals rely on heavy integration fabrics, multi-layer coordinators, and deep telemetry pipelines that hinder deployability and amplify coordination overhead. We propose a lightweight, decentralized conversation
case_studies.summary: This research aims to solve the problem of complex service provisioning in Organic 6G networks by building a lightweight, decentralized conversational orchestration system. The result is a more scalable and agile system for managing networks. This is not directly relevant to current IT infrastructure work as it focuses on future 6G networks.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work as it focuses on future 6G networks. If your organization is involved in 6G research or development, you may want to review this research for potential future applications. No immediate action is required for current cloud infrastructure management.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty: 28 - proposes a lightweight, decentralized conversation orchestration approach for Organic 6G networks. Relevant to IT engineers working on edge-computing and cloud infrastructure. 90-day value: 17 - an IT engineer might find this interesting but unlikely to directly affect their daily work or client projects.

case_studies.title: Massive Activations in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models: Pre-Attention Spikes and Inter-Spike Plateaus
case_studies.abstract: We present the first systematic study of Massive activations (MAs) in layer-interleaved HLA LLMs and uncover two architecture-aligned morphologies: MAs consistently spike immediately before full attention layers, forming pre-attention spikes (PAS), and can persist through intervening linear attention layers, giving rise to inter-spike plateaus (ISP). As full attention becomes denser, successive PAS become increasingly connected through ISP, ultimately recovering the stable MA morphology of full attention LLMs. We establish the recurrence of this organization across five linear attention archit
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of understanding massive activations in hybrid linear attention large language models, presenting a study that built a systematic analysis of these models and resulted in the discovery of two architecture-aligned morphologies. The study found that massive activations consistently spike before full attention layers and can persist through intervening linear attention layers. This discovery can help improve the understanding and development of large language models.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on the development and analysis of large language models, but IT consultants working with AI and machine learning may find the research relevant for future implementations.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Paper reveals novel details about Large Language models but lacks IT angle and actionable insights. Novelty is high within academic context but does not impact IT engineers directly. Value within 90 days is limited.

case_studies.title: Deployment Decision Reliability: A Generalizability-Theory Framework for Sizing Long-Horizon Agent Evaluations
case_studies.abstract: Enterprise practitioners read agent leaderboards as if they ranked agent capability. We show, across three open agent-trace benchmarks (TheAgentCompany, $τ^2$-bench, and AppWorld), that the agent main effect accounts for less than 3% of total variance in every dataset and check type, while the agent-by-task interaction accounts for 7-23%. Leaderboards rank specialization, not capability. We arrive at this through a four-facet Generalizability Theory variance decomposition, fit with three estimators (Henderson Method-I, REML via lme4, and a Bayesian binomial GLMM) that agree to three decimal pl
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of unreliable agent evaluations by showing that leaderboards often measure specialization, not capability. The authors built a Generalizability Theory framework to analyze agent evaluations across three benchmarks. The result shows that the agent's interaction with tasks has a much larger impact on performance than the agent itself.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on agent evaluations in a research context.
case_studies.score_reasoning: The paper reveals something about leaderboards in agent evaluations, which might affect how IT engineers and consultants in specific domains use AI, but it's not directly relevant to the average IT engineer or consultant. The concepts might be relevant to those working on developing custom AI models for enterprise use, but general applicability is unclear.

case_studies.title: Making Collaborative Signals Count: Graph-Aware Large Language Models for Sequential Recommendation
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have been widely adopted as backbones for recommender systems. However, their language-centric pretraining makes it difficult to capture collaborative signals implicit in user-item interactions, which are crucial for personalized recommendation. Existing methods either inject collaborative representations produced by external recommenders or model only intra-sequence dependencies, limiting their ability to exploit global collaborative patterns. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of capturing collaborative signals in user-item interactions for personalized recommendations by building a graph-aware large language model framework called GALLM. The result is a framework that can better exploit global collaborative patterns for sequential recommendation. This research is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work
case_studies.score_reasoning: Paper shows Novelty as large language models are widely adopted, but its IT relevance is limited as it's a recommender system framework. Value score is high due to potential for automation in similar domains.
